newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Henderson Land earnings growth seen strong.
newsitem.headline: Henderson Land earnings growth seen strong.

text.p: Henderson Land Development Co Ltd is expected to post solid earnings in the year ahead, with its large land bank and high margin property sales providing a continued source of growth, analysts said on Thursday.
Henderson Land reported fiscal 1996 net profit of HK$8.36 billion on Wednesday, up from HK$7.03 billion the previous year.
Analysts had expected net profit of about HK$8.0 billion.
"For 1997, I expect very strong growth to maybe HK$10 billion based on strong property sales mainly and growing rental income as well," said Desmond Cheung, analyst at Vickers Ballas.
Henderson Land said developments completed during fiscal 1996 brought in very substantial profits. "The group's rental income continues to increase," it added.
Henderson Land also said "stable and satisfactory growth" was expected in the coming financial year.

Analysts said Henderson Land's Metro City development and Tolo Place property developments in Hong Kong's rapidly developing New Territories were expected to contribute a large portion of fiscal 1997 earnings.
"These two projects alone will contribute a pre-tax profit of HK$ 7.8 billion," said Edward Chan, research director at Standard Chartered Securities.
"We expect about 55 percent of the development profit to be booked in 1997 from these two projects has been already locked in after the pre-sales over the last six months," he said.
Henderson Land said it has received an "overwhelming response" to the pre-sale of its first phase of Metro City.

"Sales results have been very satisfactory with sales prices of the residential units actually recorded at 15 percent to 20 percent higher than those originally estimated at this time last year," Henderson said.
"Moreover, sale of other development projects of the group has also progressed well and increase in sale prices and good turnover have also been recorded," it added.
Standard Chartered's Chan forecast 1996/97 net profit of HK$10.9 billion.

"Last year they completed about 1.8 million square feet of development properties and in 1997 we expect the size will be about 2.7 million square feet. We expect total development profit to be about HK$10 billion at the pre tax level," he said.

He said rental income should continue strong. "In 1996 it increased by 37 percent to HK$1.2 billion. Next year the commercial arcades in Metro City will be opened in phases so we expect rental income to increase quite sharply too," Chan said.
Analysts said profit margins were expected to remain high since Henderson had kept land costs at low levels.
"They have a very low cost land bank and that is why they will continue to enjoy quite a high profit margin," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
"They still have quite a number of projects to be available for sale in the coming year because they are continuing to replenish their land bank," he added.

Henderson said in a letter to shareholders that it had "a large development land bank in hand acquired at relatively low acquisition costs". It said its total development land bank in Hong Kong amounted to about 24.2 million square feet in total attributable gross floor area.
Analysts said the company's focus on the residential area would also help earnings.

"We are quite positive for further capital value appreciation in the residential market, so that being the case I think both earnings upgrades and NAV (net asset value) upgrades are likely through the coming 12 months,"said Andrew Taylor, analyst at Asia Equity.
